title: America Shouldn’t Let Go of the Middle East
gist: Philip Gordon argues that US presidents since Clinton have repeatedly promised to leave the Middle East and been pulled back in, and that disengagement is not the answer. Only the opening is available (paywall).

themes.theme: US pull-back from the Middle East

insights.claim: Every American president of the past three decades has tried to reduce US involvement in the Middle East and been drawn back in, as Clinton did with the Israeli-Palestinian conflict and Iraq, and George W. Bush did with Afghanistan and Iraq.
insights.speaker: Philip H. Gordon
insights.so_what: Suggests announced US retrenchment from the region tends not to hold, so risk models should not assume permanent disengagement.
insights.quote: Just when I thought I was out, they pull me back in.

insights.claim: The author's title argues that America should not let go of the Middle East and that disengagement is not the answer.
insights.speaker: Philip H. Gordon
insights.so_what: Signals continued US military and diplomatic presence in the region as the base case.
insights.quote: Why Disengagement Is Not the Answer
